transcription.text: This is the long speech test for the ears.
The work computer is reading a single paragraph out loud, without stopping, so that the listening
computer hears more than one minute of speech in one piece.
The river runs past the old mill, where the wheel still turns slowly in the morning light,
and the miller counts the sacks of grain one by one before the carts arrive from the village.
Every cart has two horses, and every horse has a name, and the children shout the names
as the carts roll over the wooden bridge.
After the bridge the road climbs into the hills, past the orchards and the stone walls, past
the chapel with the green door, and on toward the market town where the bells ring every
In the market there are apples and cheese, bread and honey, wool and robe, and a man who sells
clocks that all show a different time.
The test continues for a little while longer, so that the piece is long enough, and then
the speaker stops and the room is quiet.
On the way home the carts are lighter, the horses walk faster, and the children fall asleep
